items.title: Java4Shell update: attackers are now probing for the critical Java flaw
items.why: Scanners and early exploit attempts are hitting servers running OpenJDK 17+, with no confirmed break-ins yet. Keycloak, Amazon, Microsoft and Azul now have patched builds; Cisco has no fix yet.
items.action: Update Java to the November 17 builds now, starting with internet-facing Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Keycloak and Elasticsearch, and follow vendor workarounds where no patch exists.

items.title: Critical VMware vCenter flaw lets attackers skip login over the network
items.why: Broadcom fixed an authentication bypass rated 9.8 in vCenter 8.0, 9.0 and 9.1 and related VCF products. No attacks yet, but similar vCenter bugs from July were used to deploy ransomware on ESXi hosts.
items.action: Patch vCenter to Broadcom's fixed build as an emergency change, and make sure vCenter is only reachable from your admin network, never the internet.

items.title: F5 patches five critical NGINX flaws as exploit code goes public
items.why: The 'NGINX2Root' bugs allow unauthenticated remote code execution in NGINX Open Source and Plus, two of them via HTTP/2. F5 reports no attacks, but proof-of-concept code is out and Censys counts about 9 million exposed servers.
items.action: Upgrade NGINX to 1.30.7 or 1.31.9 (Plus 37.0.8.1 or 37.3.0.1), or ask your host to; if you cannot yet, turn off HTTP/2.

items.title: CISA says a Synology NAS flaw is being exploited, with ransomware hitting the devices
items.why: CISA added an unauthenticated takeover flaw in Synology DSM to its exploited list on November 18; recent attacks on Synology boxes have deployed C3RB3R ransomware. Apache Axis, REDCap and LiteLLM flaws were added too.
items.action: Update every Synology NAS to the latest DSM release, take it off the open internet, and confirm your backups are not reachable from the NAS itself.

items.title: N-able confirms hackers got into its Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud
items.why: An intruder accessed a server in N-able's hosted email filtering cloud, knocking out the admin portal, quarantine and logs in the Americas, Europe and APAC since November 16. Mail filtering still works; no data theft found so far.
items.action: Ask your MSP or N-able whether you are affected, watch for spam and phishing that quarantine would normally catch, and reset any admin passwords for the portal once it returns.

items.title: PHP fixes seven critical flaws; updates for all supported versions are out
items.why: Updated: the promised PHP release shipped today, fixing seven critical bugs ranging from remote code execution to crashes in PHP 8.2 through 8.5. No attacks reported yet. This affects most WordPress and PHP sites.
items.action: Ask your web host or developer to move PHP to 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 or 8.5.13 on every site this week.
